notes:
Idiom rating: ACCEPTABLE — Three real issues remain: SetError::with_properties takes Vec<String> forcing callers to write vec\!["x".to_owned()] (API inconsistency with with_description); find_immutable_patch_key returns Option<String> when Option<&'static str> would avoid allocations; role uniqueness check allocates two Strings per comparison in O(mailboxes) loop. No unsafe, no unwrap without justification, no dead code. The rest of the codebase is clean idiomatic Rust.
Rust idiom confidence: 90% chance of no missed issues. Least confident flags: role comparison (JMAP-2qp.6) — depends on whether MailboxRole implements Display/PartialEq<str>; if it does, the idiomatic fix is straightforward, if not the to_string() comparison may be intentional. Uncertainty driven by: not reading the jmap-mail-types crate for MailboxRole trait bounds.
Maintainer risk: MEDIUM — Identity/set update accepts server-set fields (mayDelete, id) in patch, forwarding them to backend without rejection. Naive backends silently accept client-controlled server-set fields.
Confidence: 85% chance of no missed bugs. Least confident flags: Email/copy created response format (RFC says server-set props only but text is ambiguous about whether full object is permitted); anchor handling (verified absent, may have been intentionally deferred). Uncertainty driven by: could not run tests against live RFC conformance suite; integration test file was too large to read in full. Would raise confidence if: integration tests explicitly cover anchor/anchorOffset (anchorNotFound), collapseThreads in queryChanges, total field gating in queryChanges, and Email/import created response field set.
